translation:
Once, families of uda-bhakts lived in villages very close to Shahpura and Puniyad. These families lived in villages along the banks of the Dhadhar river. Jivanji Maharaj would meet them again and again, so that they could get the opportunity to hear his words and to serve him. In the same way, at that time, uda-bhakt families also lived in the village of Thuvavi, near Bhilapur. At present, apart from Bhilapur, bhakt families live only in Beharampur; the rest of the families have migrated elsewhere.

At one time, Jivanji Maharaj came to Bhilapur, to the house of the devotee Bhagwanbhai, and a night-time satsang and bhajan gathering was arranged there. All the devotees from the surrounding villages gathered together, sang hari-kirtan, and took the benefit of the Guru's words. It was the monsoon season, and rain was falling. At that time, the loving devotee women living in Thuvavi prepared sukhdi (a sweet) as prasad and were eager to give it to Jivanji Maharaj to offer to God. But after evening fell, with the rain pouring down, the Dhadhar river, which flows between Bhilapur and Thuvavi, threatened to become an obstacle. If the river's waters rose, it would become difficult to cross to the far bank. These sisters' devotion was strong, and their resolve too was powerful. They resolved, even at the risk of danger, to cross the river. Taking the sukhdi prasad, they arrived at the riverbank.
